[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.

To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.

Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.

> **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.

46	## Or adopt by hand
47	
48	To adopt an existing app by hand:
49	
50	1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
51	2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. 52	3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
53	4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
54	
55	Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. 57	## Enable Partial Prefetching
58	
59	> **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
60	
61	Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
62	
63	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
64	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
65	
66	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
67	  cacheComponents: true,
68	  partialPrefetching: true,
69	}
70	
71	export default nextConfig
72	```
73	
74	After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
75	
76	> **Good to know**: When `cacheComponents` is enabled without a `partialPrefetching` value, Next.js logs a warning asking you to set it to `true` or `false`. Set `false` only to keep the previous prefetch behavior while you work through this guide. Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.
77	
78	## What changes for `<Link>`
79	
80	| `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
81	| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
82	| `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
83	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
84	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
85	
86	The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
87	
88	## Migrate existing full prefetches
89	
90	Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
91	
92	A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
93	
94	> **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. Only `params` and `searchParams` are [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), which varies per link and can't be included in the shared App Shell.

97	
98	To verify the migration programmatically, an [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) test can capture the UI that should stay available from an existing full prefetch. 102	import { instant } from '@next/playwright'
103	
104	test('preserves the prefetched product summary', async ({ page }) => {
105	  await page.goto('/products')
106	
107	  await instant(page, async () => {
108	    const link = page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
109	    await expect(link).toBeVisible()
110	    await link.click()
111	    await page.waitForURL((url) => url.pathname === '/products/baseball-cap')

113	    await expect(

115	    ).toBeVisible()

117	  })
118	})

274	### URL data
275	
276	[URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. The links keep `prefetch={true}`, and [Prefetching URL data](#prefetching-url-data) covers prefetching the content ahead of the click.
277	
278	### Real-time content
279	
280	A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.
281	
282	| Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
283	| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
284	| [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
285	| [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
286	| [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
287	| [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
288	| [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |

595	
596	The `prefetch` route segment config controls how a segment is prefetched during client-side navigation. By default, the framework manages the strategy based on the app's [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) setting. To override per segment, set this export to one of the values below.
597	
598	> **Good to know**:
599	>
600	> - The `prefetch` export only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
601	> - `prefetch` cannot be used when the segment is a Client Component.
602	> - The meaningful values to set are `'partial'` and `'force-disabled'`. `'auto'` is the default and is equivalent to omitting the export; don't write `prefetch = 'auto'` explicitly.
603	> - A `page` or `layout` that also calls the [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch) function needs to import it under another name, for example `import { prefetch as prefetchStage } from 'next/cache'`.
604	
605	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx" switcher
606	export const prefetch = 'partial'
607	
608	export default function Page() {
609	  return <div>...</div>
610	}
611	```

621	## Options
622	
623	### `'partial'`
624	
625	Opts the segment into [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) without enabling the global [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) flag. A `<Link>` pointing at a segment with `prefetch = 'partial'` loads the per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) instead of the legacy full prefetch. Set this on the destination, not the link.
626	
627	For links that opt into a wider prefetch with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch), Next.js uses per-link prefetching. The server renders a fresh response that resolves URL data (`params`, `searchParams`, and the full URL). On pages where all the content is statically renderable, Next.js serves prefetches from the static cache. If a page accesses non-static data, it's prefetched at runtime.
628	
629	Use this for incremental adoption when you can't enable `partialPrefetching` for the entire app at once. Once every route in scope has `prefetch = 'partial'`, enable the global flag and remove the per-route exports.
630	
631	> **Good to know**: When Next.js performs a per-link prefetch for a segment, all downstream segments are included in the same request. Segments deeper in the tree that are configured with `'force-disabled'` will still be prefetched as part of the response.
632	
633	```tsx filename="page.tsx"
634	export const prefetch = 'partial'
635	```
636	
637	### `'force-disabled'`
638	
639	Never prefetch this segment. The client will not request segment data ahead of navigation. Use this for segments where prefetching would be wasteful, for example pages behind authentication that are rarely visited.
640	
641	> **Good to know**: `'force-disabled'` does not prevent Next.js from prefetching metadata about the route. However, the actual segment data for this segment and all deeper segments will be omitted from prefetching.
642	
643	## Relationship with the `<Link prefetch>` prop
644	
645	A prefetch starts with a `<Link>` that expresses intent (should this destination be prefetched, and how eagerly), and ends at a segment that sets a cost ceiling (how much work is it OK to do ahead of time, for any link that points here).
646	
647	A destination can't know which links target it, so the segment config caps what any `<Link prefetch={true}>` pulls:
648	
649	- [`'partial'`](#partial): App Shell for default links; a `<Link prefetch={true}>` additionally resolves URL data (`params`, `searchParams`, and the full URL) and the cached content behind it.
650	- [`'force-disabled'`](#force-disabled): skip segment data entirely.
651	
652	`<Link prefetch={false}>` skips prefetching at the link level regardless of how the destination is configured.
653	
654	> **Good to know**: On pages where all the content is statically renderable, Next.js serves prefetches from the static cache (or a CDN). If a page accesses non-static data like cookies or headers, it's prefetched at runtime with a fresh server render, which costs server CPU per page view.

682	Calling `await prefetch()` keeps runtime work below it out of the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). 686	## Usage
687	
688	The function requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) and throws an error if not enabled. Without [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) a route has no App Shell, so the function has no effect. Enable Partial Prefetching globally, or one route at a time, by [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching).
689	
690	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={4,5}
691	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
692	
693	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
694	  cacheComponents: true,
695	  partialPrefetching: true,
696	}
697	
698	export default nextConfig
699	```
700	
701	With Partial Prefetching enabled, Next.js loads server-rendered output in stages, before and during a client navigation. These are the route's [navigation stages](/docs/app/glossary#navigation-stages):
702	
703	1. A default `<Link>` loads the App Shell, which holds the part of the route that does not depend on the URL.
704	2. An optional [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch), or [`router.prefetch(href, { kind: 'full' })`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-router), can also load content that depends on the link's URL.
705	3. When the user follows the link, the navigation renders the rest of the route.
706	
707	During runtime rendering, awaiting `prefetch()` keeps content out of the App Shell, so it renders during a per-link prefetch or navigation. Static prerenders can still include the content.
708	
709	Calling `router.prefetch(href)` without `kind: 'full'` requests only the App Shell under Partial Prefetching. It does not render content below `await prefetch()`.
710	
711	To keep content out of per-link prefetches as well, so it renders only on the navigation, use [`navigation()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation).
712	
713	> **Good to know**: `prefetch()` defers one subtree. To require a static App Shell across the route, use [`ensureStatic = 'shell'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/ensureStatic#shell). See [Keeping pages static](/docs/app/guides/keeping-pages-static) for a worked example.

788	  const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value
789	  return db.recommendations.rank({ session })
790	}
791	```
792	
793	The greeting reads the session and stays in the App Shell. The recommendations read it too, inside `getRecommendations`, so that read is deferred along with the ranking. Remove `prefetch()` and they become part of the App Shell that every link into the route loads.
794	
795	Put the directive on a function called below it, as `getRecommendations` does here. Awaiting `prefetch()` inside a cached scope, such as [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or [`use cache: private`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private), is not allowed.
796	
797	## How `prefetch()` differs from `connection()`
798	
799	The [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) function waits for a real request. It excludes the code that follows from prerendering and prefetching, making that work request-dependent.
800	
801	Awaiting `prefetch()` excludes the code that follows from the App Shell. It can resolve during a per-link prefetch without making that work request-dependent. A function called after `await prefetch()` can therefore use [`"use cache"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and keep its cache lifetime without generating its result for every link into the route.
802	
803	Use `connection()` when the work must run for a real request. Use `prefetch()` when the work is reusable but should only run for a selected per-link prefetch or a navigation.
804	
805	## When to use it
806	
807	Use `prefetch()` when the content below it is expensive to produce and should not be generated in the App Shell that every `<Link>` into the route loads.
808	
809	Producing the App Shell does not run that code, so its upstream requests are not issued until a per-link prefetch or the navigation.
810	
811	Leaving content uncached also keeps it out of the shell, but gives up its cache lifetime and cannot make it available during a per-link prefetch. With `prefetch()`, the content can be cached with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or [`use cache: private`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private), given a lifetime, and deferred to a per-link prefetch or navigation.
812	
813	Uncached reads, values with a short [`stale`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#stale) time, and anything behind `params` or `searchParams` are already left out of the shell on their own.
814	
815	### Keeping the App Shell static
816	
817	When every read of [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) and [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) sits below `prefetch()`, the prerender a shell prefetch would trigger cannot produce more than the static output the build already generated, so the shell is served from that output instead. Shaping a route this way is an optional optimization: a static response can be cached in a CDN, so a default `<Link>` into the route costs no server CPU at all. A route that resolves `params` or `searchParams` gets that prerender instead, and so does the example above: its greeting reads the session in the shell, so the shell renders once per visitor and only the recommendations are deferred.
818	
819	## Good to know
820	
821	- The function has no effect on the initial load of a page.
822	- Unlike [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection), it does not mark the subtree as request-dependent. Content below `await prefetch()` stays fully cacheable and can be wrapped in [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache).
823	- A call outside a `<Suspense>` boundary surfaces an [Instant Insight](/docs/messages/instant-navigation-stage) in development. A fully prerendered route is unaffected, but the insight identifies that the call would defer content without a fallback if the route later requires runtime rendering.
824	- Calling it inside `use cache`, `use cache: private`, [`unstable_cache()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_cache), [`after()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/after), [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params), or a Client Component throws.
825	- In a `page` or `layout` that sets the [`prefetch` route segment config](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch), import the function under another name, for example `import { prefetch as prefetchStage } from 'next/cache'`, since both are named `prefetch`.
826	
827	## Reference
828	
829	### Type
830	
831	```ts
832	function prefetch(): Promise<void>
833	```
834	
835	### Parameters
836	
837	- The function does not accept any parameters.
838	
839	### Returns
840	
841	A `Promise<void>`. It is not meant to be consumed.
842	
843	## Version History
844	
845	| Version   | Changes                                                                                        |
846	| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
847	| `v16.4.0` | `prefetch` introduced, replacing the `unstable_prefetch` name used in earlier canary releases. |

57	## Enable Partial Prefetching
58	
59	> **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
60	
61	Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
62	
63	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
64	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
65	
66	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
67	  cacheComponents: true,
68	  partialPrefetching: true,
69	}
70	
71	export default nextConfig
72	```
73	
74	After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
75	
76	> **Good to know**: When `cacheComponents` is enabled without a `partialPrefetching` value, Next.js logs a warning asking you to set it to `true` or `false`. 77	
78	## What changes for `<Link>`
79	
80	| `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
81	| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
82	| `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
83	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
84	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
85	
86	The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.

88	## Migrate existing full prefetches
89	
90	Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
91	
92	A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
93	
94	> **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. 275	
276	[URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. 278	### Real-time content

595	
596	The `prefetch` route segment config controls how a segment is prefetched during client-side navigation. By default, the framework manages the strategy based on the app's [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) setting. To override per segment, set this export to one of the values below.
597	
598	> **Good to know**:
599	>
600	> - The `prefetch` export only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
601	> - `prefetch` cannot be used when the segment is a Client Component.
602	> - The meaningful values to set are `'partial'` and `'force-disabled'`. `'auto'` is the default and is equivalent to omitting the export; don't write `prefetch = 'auto'` explicitly.
603	> - A `page` or `layout` that also calls the [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch) function needs to import it under another name, for example `import { prefetch as prefetchStage } from 'next/cache'`.
604	
605	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx" switcher
606	export const prefetch = 'partial'
607	
608	export default function Page() {
609	  return <div>...</div>
610	}
611	```
612	
613	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js" switcher
614	export const prefetch = 'partial'
615	
616	export default function Page() {
617	  return <div>...</div>
618	}
619	```
620	
621	## Options
622	
623	### `'partial'`
624	
625	Opts the segment into [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) without enabling the global [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) flag. A `<Link>` pointing at a segment with `prefetch = 'partial'` loads the per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) instead of the legacy full prefetch. Set this on the destination, not the link.
626	
627	For links that opt into a wider prefetch with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch), Next.js uses per-link prefetching. The server renders a fresh response that resolves URL data (`params`, `searchParams`, and the full URL). On pages where all the content is statically renderable, Next.js serves prefetches from the static cache. If a page accesses non-static data, it's prefetched at runtime.
628	
629	Use this for incremental adoption when you can't enable `partialPrefetching` for the entire app at once. Once every route in scope has `prefetch = 'partial'`, enable the global flag and remove the per-route exports.
630	
631	> **Good to know**: When Next.js performs a per-link prefetch for a segment, all downstream segments are included in the same request. Segments deeper in the tree that are configured with `'force-disabled'` will still be prefetched as part of the response.
632	
633	```tsx filename="page.tsx"
634	export const prefetch = 'partial'
635	```
636	
637	### `'force-disabled'`
638	
639	Never prefetch this segment. The client will not request segment data ahead of navigation. Use this for segments where prefetching would be wasteful, for example pages behind authentication that are rarely visited.
640	
641	> **Good to know**: `'force-disabled'` does not prevent Next.js from prefetching metadata about the route. However, the actual segment data for this segment and all deeper segments will be omitted from prefetching.
642	
643	## Relationship with the `<Link prefetch>` prop
644	
645	A prefetch starts with a `<Link>` that expresses intent (should this destination be prefetched, and how eagerly), and ends at a segment that sets a cost ceiling (how much work is it OK to do ahead of time, for any link that points here).
646	
647	A destination can't know which links target it, so the segment config caps what any `<Link prefetch={true}>` pulls:
648	
649	- [`'partial'`](#partial): App Shell for default links; a `<Link prefetch={true}>` additionally resolves URL data (`params`, `searchParams`, and the full URL) and the cached content behind it.
650	- [`'force-disabled'`](#force-disabled): skip segment data entirely.
651	
652	`<Link prefetch={false}>` skips prefetching at the link level regardless of how the destination is configured.
653	
654	> **Good to know**: On pages where all the content is statically renderable, Next.js serves prefetches from the static cache (or a CDN). If a page accesses non-static data like cookies or headers, it's prefetched at runtime with a fresh server render, which costs server CPU per page view.
655	
656	## TypeScript
657	
658	```tsx
659	type Prefetch = 'auto' | 'partial' | 'force-disabled'
660	
661	export const prefetch: Prefetch = 'partial'
662	```

681	
682	Calling `await prefetch()` keeps runtime work below it out of the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). The work can run during a per-link prefetch or navigation, while the fallback of the nearest [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary renders in the shell.
683	
684	Use `prefetch()` for content that the App Shell would otherwise render but that is expensive to generate. Static prerenders still include the content in their output.
685	
686	## Usage
687	
688	The function requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) and throws an error if not enabled. Without [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) a route has no App Shell, so the function has no effect. Enable Partial Prefetching globally, or one route at a time, by [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching).
689	
690	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={4,5}
691	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
692	
693	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
694	  cacheComponents: true,
695	  partialPrefetching: true,
696	}
697	
698	export default nextConfig
699	```
700	
701	With Partial Prefetching enabled, Next.js loads server-rendered output in stages, before and during a client navigation. These are the route's [navigation stages](/docs/app/glossary#navigation-stages):
702	
703	1. A default `<Link>` loads the App Shell, which holds the part of the route that does not depend on the URL.
704	2. An optional [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch), or [`router.prefetch(href, { kind: 'full' })`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-router), can also load content that depends on the link's URL.
705	3. When the user follows the link, the navigation renders the rest of the route.
706	
707	During runtime rendering, awaiting `prefetch()` keeps content out of the App Shell, so it renders during a per-link prefetch or navigation. Static prerenders can still include the content.
708	
709	Calling `router.prefetch(href)` without `kind: 'full'` requests only the App Shell under Partial Prefetching. It does not render content below `await prefetch()`.
710	
711	To keep content out of per-link prefetches as well, so it renders only on the navigation, use [`navigation()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation).
712	
713	> **Good to know**: `prefetch()` defers one subtree. To require a static App Shell across the route, use [`ensureStatic = 'shell'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/ensureStatic#shell). See [Keeping pages static](/docs/app/guides/keeping-pages-static) for a worked example.
714	
715	Everything above `prefetch()` renders in the App Shell, and everything below renders on a per-link prefetch or on the navigation. Deferral is scoped to the component that awaits it and the tree below: sibling branches render in the shell as usual. Place it above the work to defer, and wrap the component in [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense):
716	
717	```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" highlight={25} switcher
718	import { Suspense } from 'react'
719	import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
720	import { cacheLife, prefetch } from 'next/cache'
721	
722	export default function Page() {
723	  return (
724	    <>
725	      <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading greeting...</p>}>
726	        <Greeting /> {/* in the App Shell */}
727	      </Suspense>
728	      <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading recommendations...</p>}>
729	        {/* the fallback is in the App Shell, the recommendations are not */}
730	        <Recommendations />
731	      </Suspense>
732	    </>
733	  )
734	}
735	
736	async function Greeting() {
737	  const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value
738	  return <p>{session ? 'Welcome back' : 'Welcome'}</p>
739	}
740	
741	async function Recommendations() {
742	  await prefetch() // runtime work below renders on a per-link prefetch or navigation
743	  const items = await getRecommendations()
744	  return <List items={items} />
745	}
746	
747	async function getRecommendations() {
748	  'use cache: private'
749	  cacheLife('hours')
750	  const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value
751	  return db.recommendations.rank({ session })
752	}
753	```
754	
755	```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" highlight={25} switcher

757	import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
758	import { cacheLife, prefetch } from 'next/cache'
759	
760	export default function Page() {
761	  return (
762	    <>
763	      <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading greeting...</p>}>
764	        <Greeting /> {/* in the App Shell */}
765	      </Suspense>

767	        {/* the fallback is in the App Shell, the recommendations are not */}
768	        <Recommendations />
769	      </Suspense>
770	    </>
771	  )
772	}
773	
774	async function Greeting() {
775	  const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value
776	  return <p>{session ? 'Welcome back' : 'Welcome'}</p>
777	}
778	
779	async function Recommendations() {
780	  await prefetch() // runtime work below renders on a per-link prefetch or navigation
781	  const items = await getRecommendations()
782	  return <List items={items} />
783	}
784	
785	async function getRecommendations() {
786	  'use cache: private'
787	  cacheLife('hours')

792	
793	The greeting reads the session and stays in the App Shell. The recommendations read it too, inside `getRecommendations`, so that read is deferred along with the ranking. Remove `prefetch()` and they become part of the App Shell that every link into the route loads.
794	
795	Put the directive on a function called below it, as `getRecommendations` does here. Awaiting `prefetch()` inside a cached scope, such as [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or [`use cache: private`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private), is not allowed.
796	
797	## How `prefetch()` differs from `connection()`
798	
799	The [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) function waits for a real request. It excludes the code that follows from prerendering and prefetching, making that work request-dependent.
800	
801	Awaiting `prefetch()` excludes the code that follows from the App Shell. It can resolve during a per-link prefetch without making that work request-dependent. A function called after `await prefetch()` can therefore use [`"use cache"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and keep its cache lifetime without generating its result for every link into the route.
802	
803	Use `connection()` when the work must run for a real request. Use `prefetch()` when the work is reusable but should only run for a selected per-link prefetch or a navigation.
804	
805	## When to use it
806	
807	Use `prefetch()` when the content below it is expensive to produce and should not be generated in the App Shell that every `<Link>` into the route loads.
808	
809	Producing the App Shell does not run that code, so its upstream requests are not issued until a per-link prefetch or the navigation.
810	
811	Leaving content uncached also keeps it out of the shell, but gives up its cache lifetime and cannot make it available during a per-link prefetch. With `prefetch()`, the content can be cached with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or [`use cache: private`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private), given a lifetime, and deferred to a per-link prefetch or navigation.
812	
813	Uncached reads, values with a short [`stale`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#stale) time, and anything behind `params` or `searchParams` are already left out of the shell on their own.
814	
815	### Keeping the App Shell static
816	
817	When every read of [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) and [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) sits below `prefetch()`, the prerender a shell prefetch would trigger cannot produce more than the static output the build already generated, so the shell is served from that output instead. Shaping a route this way is an optional optimization: a static response can be cached in a CDN, so a default `<Link>` into the route costs no server CPU at all. A route that resolves `params` or `searchParams` gets that prerender instead, and so does the example above: its greeting reads the session in the shell, so the shell renders once per visitor and only the recommendations are deferred.
818	
819	## Good to know
820	
821	- The function has no effect on the initial load of a page.
822	- Unlike [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection), it does not mark the subtree as request-dependent. Content below `await prefetch()` stays fully cacheable and can be wrapped in [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache).
823	- A call outside a `<Suspense>` boundary surfaces an [Instant Insight](/docs/messages/instant-navigation-stage) in development. A fully prerendered route is unaffected, but the insight identifies that the call would defer content without a fallback if the route later requires runtime rendering.
824	- Calling it inside `use cache`, `use cache: private`, [`unstable_cache()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_cache), [`after()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/after), [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params), or a Client Component throws.
825	- In a `page` or `layout` that sets the [`prefetch` route segment config](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch), import the function under another name, for example `import { prefetch as prefetchStage } from 'next/cache'`, since both are named `prefetch`.
826

841	A `Promise<void>`. It is not meant to be consumed.

{message.body}

}> ) } async function Stories() { await navigation() const topic = (await cookies()).get('topic')?.value ?? 'all' return } ``` Reading the cookie below `navigation()` does not make the per-link prefetch render per request, because that read would not have resolved during the prefetch anyway. A fully prerendered route is unaffected, but the insight identifies that the call would defer content without a fallback if the route later requires runtime rendering. If a mutation can update the data, [tag and invalidate the cached result](/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating). Skip it when the prefetch can't produce a better UI than the App Shell. Each visible `` can wake a server, and that cost only pays off if more of the page is ready before the click: - The route has little or no URL-data dependency. The App Shell already makes the navigation instant. - The dependent content has to be fresh on every request. The prerender stops at the same `` fallback, so the user sees the same UI either way. - The route is rarely navigated to. You pay per visible link, regardless of click-through. A per-link prefetch is best-effort. It only helps the navigations where it completes before the click. On a slow connection, on a feed of many links, or on a direct visit, it may not be ready when the user navigates, and the navigation falls back to the App Shell. When many links to a route are visible at once, such as a grid of cards, each `` prefetches that link's content as it enters the viewport, so the grid makes one such server request per card. Related products are now left out of the default prefetch for `/product`. The featured-product link loads them before the click, so they show immediately when you navigate from it. I checked this in a production build but not by clicking through in a browser.

**Changes:**

- **`next.config.ts`**: turned on `partialPrefetching: true`. With it on, a normal `<Link>` downloads only the page's shared base layer, which Next.js calls the "App Shell". Without it, the `prefetch()` call below does nothing.
- **`app/product/page.tsx`**: moved the related-products list into its own `<RelatedProducts>` component and wrapped it in `<Suspense>` with a "Loading related products..." placeholder. The component calls `await prefetch()` from `next/cache` before it fetches anything. That keeps the list out of the default prefetch, which gets the placeholder instead. `getRelatedProducts()` keeps its `'use cache'` with the `hours` lifetime.
- **`app/page.tsx`**: the featured-product link now has `prefetch={true}`. That link loads the full page, including the related products, before the click.

**How I checked it:** `next build` succeeds and `/product` is still fully static (revalidates every hour). In the built prefetch file for the page, the default prefetch is cut off at byte 3081. That part contains the heading, the description and the loading placeholder. "Compact Widget" first appears at byte 3151, past the cut-off, so a normal link doesn't get it. The featured link reads the whole file, so it does.

**Things to know:**
- Because the page is fully static, the featured link's fuller prefetch is served from static output and doesn't run the server.
- Anyone who reaches `/product` through any other link will see the loading placeholder briefly before the list appears.
- The build rewrote `tsconfig.json` (`jsx: react-jsx`, plus an extra `include` entry). I reverted that and deleted the build output and the generated `next-env.d.ts`, so only the three files above changed. The next build will make the same `tsconfig.json` changes again.
